title: Active Convulsions / Seizure Management
source_citation: International Federation of Red Cross and Red Crescent Societies (IFRC) International First Aid Guidelines 2020; Epilepsy Foundation Clinical First Aid Protocols

steps.text_key: Call 112 immediately if this is a first seizure, lasts longer than 5 minutes, repeats, or the person was injured
Time the seizure: note the exact start time of active jerking or convulsions
Protect from harm: gently guide them away from hazards, move furniture, and cushion their head with something soft (folded jacket)
Loosen tight clothing around the neck to assist airway and breathing
Once active convulsive jerking stops: gently turn the person onto their side into the recovery position to keep airway clear of saliva or vomit
Stay with the person until they are fully awake and their breathing has returned to normal; speak reassuringly

do_not: Do not restrain the person's movements or pin them down during active convulsions
Do not place any object, spoon, finger, or medication into the person's mouth
Do not give any food, water, or pills until the person is completely conscious and alert
Do not attempt CPR during an active convulsion unless they remain completely unresponsive and not breathing after the seizure stops
